audit.why: 54.02% over 224 games with a Lillia window at 3-5 and a Ryze item flip after it is an even lane; the mirror left difficulty untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 read Lillia in both layers while whys[0], spikes[0] and early all say Ryze has the range edge and should deny her early stacks.
audit.why: Overload is 1000 range; Blooming Blows is a 450-range self-cast she has to walk in for. The packet says Ryze and the mirror already flipped its side of this row.
audit.corrected: phases[0]/win[0] Lillia -> Ryze with rating 4/10 -> 6/10, as a matched pair. Rows 3 and 4-5 left as they are so the two directions stay identical — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: early contains a confused parenthetical — 'she has W (Swirlseed), E (Whimsy is her R, so her W is the AOE slam)'. Swirlseed is E, the AoE slam is W (Watch Out! Eep!), and 'Whimsy' belongs to a different champion entirely. wants.foe[2] calls her W 'longer-reaching' than your root; W is 500, your Rune Prison is 615. late claims your root reapplies 'every two seconds' — Rune Prison is 11 down to 9.
audit.why: Two of the three are advice-changing: a player told to fear a longer-ranged W will hold spacing at the wrong distance, and 'root every two seconds' promises a lock that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Slots named correctly (Q Blooming Blows 450, W Watch Out! Eep! 500 on 14-10s, E Swirlseed 700 flat 12s, R Lilting Lullaby 150s), and the root cycle stated at its real 9-11 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Blows' outer edge deals true damage and the page never says so; nor does it mention Swirlseed rolling until it hits a wall.
audit.why: True damage means stacking MR is the wrong read on her burn, and a rolling seed can cut a retreat you have no dash to answer.
audit.corrected: True damage folded into spikes[1], the rolling seed into wants.foe[2] and mid.

edits.before: Lillia's Blooming Blows stack speed and W-E kite loop peak here — her DOT cycling punishes any static trade while your mana costs are highest.
edits.after: Blooming Blows is 6s at rank 1 and its outer edge lands true damage, so resists never answer it — her kite loop peaks while your mana costs are highest.

edits.before: Avoid your W root entirely by using her passive-speed movement to stay at the outer edge of E range and trade only with her longer-reaching W
edits.after: Stay past your 615 range on stacked move speed and poke with Swirlseed, a flat 12-second roll that keeps going until it hits a wall or you

edits.before: At level 1 Ryze has the edge — Q poke reaches farther than Lillia needs to get to land Blooming Blows, so chip her every time she walks up to last-hit and deny the stacks that power her passive move speed loop. The danger starts at level 3: once she has W (Swirlseed), E (Whimsy is her R, so her W is the AOE slam), and her passive DOT cycling, she can run circles around a stationary trade and walk away faster than Phase Rush fires. Do not auto-commit; trade only when you have E up to Flux a minion beside her, then W root through the wave bounce. If her Blooming Blows is already stacked, respect it — her move speed in that state lets her kite your empowered Q before it hits.
edits.after: At level 1 Ryze has the edge — Overload reaches 1000 while Blooming Blows is a 450-range self-cast she must walk in for, so chip her every time she steps up to last-hit and deny the stacks that power her move speed. The danger starts at level 3: with Watch Out! Eep! slamming at 500, Swirlseed rolling from 700, and her passive burning over time, she can circle a stationary trade and leave faster than Phase Rush fires. Do not auto-commit; trade only with E up to Flux a minion beside her, then Rune Prison through the wave bounce. If her speed is already stacked, respect it — she kites your empowered Overload before it lands.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are her lane — high mana costs mean your rotations are incomplete, and she can cycle Blooming Blows DOT with her W slam and walk away in the speed buff before you can chain a second root. Play the wave: slow-push a Fluxed wave and let it crash so you get recall windows, not extended trades where her sustained DOT beats your burst. At level 6 neither of you gets a combat steroid — Realm Warp adds macro threat but no 1v1 spike, and her R (Lilting Lullaby sleep) is the thing that kills you if you are caught solo out of position. Use your recall windows to buy Tear or components, and look for any opportunity to roam with Warp if she shoves you in.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are her lane — high mana costs leave your rotations incomplete, and she cycles Blooming Blows every 5 seconds behind a Watch Out! Eep! slam, leaving in the speed buff before you chain a second root. Play the wave: slow-push a Fluxed wave and crash it for recall windows, not extended trades her burn wins. At 6 neither of you gains a duel steroid — Realm Warp is macro only, and Lilting Lullaby on 150 seconds is what kills you when caught alone. Watch the walls too: a Swirlseed that misses keeps rolling and can cut the retreat you have no dash for, so hold Flash for the terrain rather than the damage.

edits.before: Rod of Ages into Seraph's is the two-item flip that makes this lane Favoured overall. Once Seraph's stacks, your mana pool feeds Arcane Mastery's AP conversion, your loop speed is near-permanent, and Lillia cannot kite a root that reapplies every two seconds. In teamfights she wants to hit the edge of her Q AOE and sleep the pile with R; you want to Realm Warp your team onto a flank angle where Lillia is in the middle of your Flux chain, not circling the outside. She never fully outscales you at two-plus items the way a hypercarrier does — the window you survived 3-5 is the only one she had.
edits.after: Rod of Ages into Seraph's is the two-item flip that makes this lane favoured overall. Once Seraph's stacks, your mana pool feeds the passive's AP conversion, Spell Flux drops to 2.5 seconds and Rune Prison to 9, and Lillia cannot kite a root coming back that fast. In teamfights she wants the true-damage edge of Blooming Blows and a Lilting Lullaby sleep on the pile; you want Realm Warp to land your team on the angle where she is inside your Flux chain, not circling it. She never outscales you at two-plus items — the window you survived at 3-5 was the only one she had.

The packet's suspectName on 'Dream-Laden Bough' in wants.foe[1] is a FALSE POSITIVE — that is the real passive name and the line is left alone. Only the Level 1 row was flipped: the mirror's audit file (audits/top/lillia__ryze.json) edits rows 0, 5 and 6 only, so flipping Levels 3 and 4-5 toward the packet here would have introduced a disagreement the mirror does not share.
